correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary fixed z in any finite-dimensional Z subset real L1, the sign identity expresses ||r_n f-z||_1 as the average of ||f-z||_1 and ||f+z||_1 plus an integral r_n(|f-z|-|f+z|)/2 that vanishes by the weak-null sign hypothesis. The limit is int max(|f|,|z|) >=||f||_1. If inf over Z fell below ||f||_1-epsilon on a subsequence, almost-minimizing z_n have L1 norm at most ||f||_1+distance and hence a convergent subsequence in the finite-dimensional kernel, contradicting fixed-z convergence. z=0 gives matching upper bound. A unit quotient coset has an attained norm-one representative by finite-dimensional coercivity; q(r_n f) is weakly null, has norm ->1 by the proved identity, and ||q(f) +/-q(r_n f)||_1 is bounded above by 1 +/- int |f|r_n ->1. Weak lower semicontinuity supplies lower limits. Covers arbitrary nonzero finite atomless mu (not requiring separability), any finite-dimensional Z, every f, both signs, and all qualifying r_n. Source Rademacher sign existence independently checked in Rodriguez--Rueda Zoca Lemma 2.1; no finite experiment substitutes for this proof.
residual_risks: Finite-dimensional kernel and real-scalar atomlessness are essential; this proof says nothing about infinite-dimensional kernels, atoms, or complex scalars.

value.rationale: The invariant question is a natural structural stability/permanence problem for a major Banach-space geometric property. It proves a kernel-independent exact norm-distance law for every finite-dimensional quotient of real nonatomic L1, not merely an isolated example; the finite-dimensional compactness mechanism resolves an actual quotient-norm obstruction. It supplies useful geometry even though the metric-graph corollary is not claimed original. Not an automatic consequence of the ambient WASQ result.
